summary: Evald Lidén was a scholar of linguistics and Indology who studied at Uppsala University (1883–1895). He served as PD of Indo-European linguistics at Uppsala (1895) and later as professor (1899) and head (1917–1929) at the University of Gothenburg.

Philosopher Evan Thompson studied at Amherst College and the University of Toronto under Robert A. F. Thurman and Francisco Varela. His career includes posts at York University (2002–2005), University of Toronto (~2005–2013), and University of British Columbia (2013).
Evelyn Frederick Charles Ludowyk was an English and history/archaeology scholar who studied at Richmond College. He served as Professor of English at the University of Ceylon from circa 1940 to 1956.

Evert Willem Beth was a Dutch philosopher who studied at Utrecht University (~1926–1935). He held positions at Johns Hopkins University (~1952–1953) and served on the faculty at the University of Amsterdam from 1946 to 1964.

Evgenij Mihajlovič Medvedev worked in Indology and history/archaeology after studying at Moscow State University (~1951–1956). He was a researcher at the Institute of Oriental Studies (1956–1957) and became Director at Moscow State University in 1960.

Eviatar Shulman is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy. He studied at the Hebrew University of Jerusalem (1998–2009), where he became Chairman of the Department of Comparative Religion in 2009.

Eyal Aviv works in Buddhist studies, Sinology, and philosophy. He earned his Ph.D. at Harvard University, studying under Robert M. Gimello, Parimal G. Patil, and Michael Puett, and held a post at George Washington University in 2014.

Indologist and linguist F. B. J. Kuiper studied at Leiden and Utrecht under Uhlenbeck, van Wijk, Caland, and Vogel. He taught at Carpentier Alting Stichting Lyceum (1934–1939) and was Professor of Sanskrit at Leiden University (1939–1972).
F. Garritsen was a scholar in the field of Indology who studied at Utrecht University under Jan Gonda.

F. Gelpke specialized in Indology and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at the University of Rostock and the University of Göttingen under Jacob Wackernagel, Hermann Oldenberg, and Emil Sieg, later serving at Berlin's Ethnological Museum (1932).

F. J. Richards worked in Indology and Indian archaeology after studying at Exeter College (1893–1902). He founded The Mythic Society in 1909 and lectured on Indian archaeology at SOAS University of London in 1931 and 1934.

F. M. G. Lorimer was a researcher in history, archaeology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. Educated at Somerville College (1902–1905), she held library posts at the Bodleian Library (1907–1909) and the Royal Asiatic Society (1932–1940).
Fa Qing is a Buddhist studies scholar who completed his doctoral studies at the University of Calgary under Leslie S. Kawamura, Anthony W. Barber, and Xiaojie Yang.
Fa Yao is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied under K. L. Dhammajoti. He is attested as a Visiting Lecturer of Theravada Buddhism at the University of Chicago for 2026.

Fabian Wilhelm af Ekenstam worked in Indology and religious studies. He studied at Lund University (fil.dr. 1808), held posts there as Docent (1809) and Adjunkt of Theology (1812), and taught philosophy at Katedralskolan, Linköping (1822–1837).

Fabienne Jagou is a scholar of Tibetology and history/archaeology. She completed her PhD at the School for Advanced Studies in the Social Sciences under Pierre-Étienne Will and became Maître de conférences at the École française d'Extrême-Orient around 2001.

Fabio Rambelli specializes in Japanology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. He studied at Ca' Foscari, Tokyo University of Foreign Studies, and Naples "L'Orientale", later holding posts at Sapporo University (2001–2002) and UC Santa Barbara (from ~2009).

Fabrizia Baldissera is an Indologist who studied at the "Federigo Enriques" Department of Mathematics (1969–2004) and held posts at the University of Florence (~2000) and the University of Naples "L'Orientale".

Fabrizio Ferrari is an Indologist and religious studies scholar educated at Ca' Foscari University of Venice and SOAS. He held posts at SOAS (2005–2008), the University of Chester (2008–2018), and the University of Padua (2018).
Fafang was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Taixu and served as a Research Fellow in Indian Buddhism at Visva-Bharati University.
